title: How do ropes and rods limit motion?
question: Along what path does a weight on a rope move, and how fast does it swing?
steps: Drag the rope's weight sideways to set the angle.
Let go and the pendulum moves.
Watch the distance from the pivot to the weight and the time of one swing there and back.
observe: See whether the rope's length stays the same as the weight moves, and whether a longer rope swings more slowly.

terms.name: Pendulum
terms.description: A thing hanging from a fixed point that swings from side to side.

terms.name: Pivot
terms.description: The point where the rope or rod is tied and does not move.

terms.name: Period
terms.description: The time to swing there and back and return to the start.

law.title: Pendulums, ropes and rods
law.description: Inside a link of fixed length, gravity makes the weight swing back and forth.

tip: Drag the blue rope weight with one finger to set the angle (5° steps) and let go: it swings. While you drag, the weight follows the white dotted path (the same distance from the pivot). Tap the weight to let it go again from the same angle.
tip_short: Drag the weight to set the angle and let go

controls.label: Damping
controls.note: The weight is 1 kg. With damping, the swing gets smaller little by little.

options.label: None
options.note: No air drag or friction: the swing stays the same

predict.question: Does a longer rope swing more slowly?
predict.reason: With a longer rope, the pendulum goes around a longer path. So one swing there and back takes longer.
predict.bridge: First swing the medium rope and watch the beat!

stages.text: On the Earth, match the turtle's beat with the medium rope!
stages.say: A ball on a rope swinging back and forth is called a **pendulum**. Gravity pulls the ball down, so the pendulum swings. Remember this beat!
stages.win: Tick-tock! You matched the turtle's beat!
stages.miss: The beat is off. Try the medium rope!

stages.text: On the Earth, make only the rope longer and match the slow beat!
stages.say: With a longer rope, the pendulum goes around a longer path. So one swing there and back takes longer.
stages.win: Tick-tock! The long rope matched the beat too!

stages.text: With the same long rope, match the very slow beat on the Moon!
stages.say: The Moon's gravity is weak, so it pulls the ball gently. So even the same rope swings very slowly on the Moon.
stages.win: The front door opened! The piece is coming out!
stages.miss: Go to the Moon with the same long rope!

story.clue: The piece is inside the turtle clock! Let's swing the ball just like the clock's pendulum!
story.map_clue: It's where a big yellow ball hangs from a post!

kid.intro: This is the swing lab. A weight on a rope swinging back and forth is called a **pendulum**. Gravity pulls the ball down. The ball comes down and goes up on the other side. Let's see how slowly it swings for each rope length!
kid.title: Let's swing a ball on a rope!
kid.say: The rope keeps its length, so the ball swings in a circle. With a longer rope, and on the Moon, it swings more slowly.
kid.tip: Drag the ball sideways and let go.

cards.small_period: There and back in a small swing

note.law: The longer the rope and the weaker the gravity, the more slowly the pendulum swings. The weight's mass does not matter.
